Chapter 9: The Ongoing Dance of Resilience.
You know, resilience isn’t something you’re just born with. It’s not a fixed part of who you are—it's a daily practice. One that’s built, little by little, through all those small choices and quiet moments where you decide to keep going.
For this mother, her son’s first year put her to the test in ways she never saw coming. But it also brought out a strength in her she never knew she had.
There were tough days—ones where nothing seemed to go right. Maybe she’d miss an appointment, or her son would melt down in the middle of the grocery store, or another long night left her barely holding on. On days like those, she honestly felt like throwing in the towel. But she didn’t. She kept moving, powered by the support of her community, the deep love for her son, and the hard-earned belief that, somehow, she could handle even the hardest moments.
One evening stands out. After a rough day, she found herself on the couch with her son, watching the colors of the sunset spill through the window. He leaned into her, his little head heavy on her shoulder. And in that simple moment, she felt a wave of gratitude. She realized that resilience isn’t about pretending things are always fine. It’s about finding a way to take the next step, even when you can’t see where the path leads.
She also started to notice, and really celebrate, the little wins—a bedtime that went smoothly, a shared laugh, a quiet hour just to breathe. These tiny moments became her milestones, proof that she was doing her best. She learned to forgive herself on the messy days and to trust that tomorrow would always bring a fresh start.
Here’s something important: she didn’t do it all on her own. Her community kept showing up—offering meals, babysitting, or just listening when she needed to vent. And she began to see that asking for help isn’t a sign of weakness. If anything, it’s a kind of wisdom.
As her son grew and needed her in new ways, she found herself letting go—of old worries, of impossible standards, of the urge to control every little thing. She started trusting her gut, tuning in to her son, and believing in their ability to figure things out as they went.
Resilience, she discovered, is a dance. It’s about stumbling and getting back up, learning and unlearning, holding on and letting go. Sure, there’d always be challenges. But now, she knew she didn’t have to face them alone. With her son and their community by her side, she could keep moving forward—one step, one day at a time.
